samples.text: The period is running on a manual arrangement while the incident remains open: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. That measure is a holding step, and nobody is treating it as a repair. Its basis is the confirmed cause, stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. Because the fault sits in reference data rather than in the valuation logic, a corrected mapping applied by hand produces a valid result for this period. The override holds only for the entries and the period it was written for. Any new mapping change made before the register is corrected falls outside it and needs the same manual treatment. For anyone deciding whether to wait, the answer is that the period valuation does not depend on a further fix. It stands on a manual correction tied to a known cause. The provisional part is the register itself, which still holds the stale entry until a permanent correction goes in. Teams can proceed on the current

The confirmed cause is stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. Legacy and cloud agency codes are both live and are not interchangeable, so a stale entry does not raise an error at the point of entry. It resolves to the wrong code, and the valuation run stops downstream. The incident was initially recorded as overnight ERP outage, and the first hours of the response followed that theory. It was ruled out on evidence: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. With the upstream system cleared, the search moved to the reference data and found the stale mapping. Under the stale entry sits a control gap, classified as control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer. The mapping error is the trigger. The missing ownership and review is the condition that let it reach production.
